_comment: Accepted cross-platform attribute-effect findings, two kinds. DIVERGENCE ({fixture, platforms}): the control-diff verdict (active = the attribute changed the render, inert = it did not) disagrees across the platforms the attribute is declared for — semantic drift unless a deliberate platform idiom; the reason says which. UNIFORMLY-INERT ({fixture, verdict, declared}): a value the SSoT enumerates changes nothing on ANY platform — either it is the default rendering (say so in the reason) or it is dead/unimplemented everywhere. Unrecorded findings fail `jui conformance gate --cross-effect`; entries the measurement no longer supports are stale and must be pruned (`jui conformance cross-effect --update`). Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the initial-measurement backlog — consume it.

measured drift, NOT accepted as correct — and the two inert platforms are NOT the same defect. iOS never reads the spelling on either path (sjui radio_converter.rb: zero `label` hits). Android reads it in CODEGEN (`text || label`) but not in the DYNAMIC component, whose declared-attribute list is group/text/icon/selectedIcon/fontColor/tintColor and which branches on `a.text` — and the fixtures render through the dynamic path, so plan 41's codegen probe passes android while the pixels do not move. The base used to supply `text`, which masked all of this as a uniform inert. Family: label-unread-spelling.

measured drift, NOT accepted (ios, android): 0 px against the control on both — pixel-exact, so this is not the dHash blindness the CI baseline lane hit on the same fixture. The Compose dynamic component derives its selection from `bind` only (literal `selectedValue` is never read), and the codegen lane agrees the spelling is unread on both platforms. Web renders it (133 px). Family: selected-state-dynamic-gap.

measured drift, NOT accepted (web): the emitted markup for the target is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the control's — no `absolute bottom-0`, no positioning class at all. rjui only emits parent-relative position classes when the PARENT is in overlay mode, and a plain View parent stays a flex column, so a child's parent-relative constraint is dropped before anything can render it. Structural container-mode change, not a one-line fix; same shape as the iOS matchParent-parent defect this plan fixed in SwiftJsonUI. Family: relative-position-container-mode.
codegen-innocent, library gap (android): the sibling constraint reaches the emitted Compose and the render does not move. ios and web place it. Family: relative-position-container-mode.

measured drift, NOT accepted as correct: same root cause as alignTop — the iOS container's default anchor is center where Compose/CSS default to start, so only iOS measures an effect. Family: gravity-default-drift.

measured drift, NOT accepted (web): same root as common/alignBottom__true — the parent never enters overlay mode, so the emitted target markup is byte-identical to the control's. Family: relative-position-container-mode.

measured drift, NOT accepted as correct: view-relative alignment against a sibling that the centered iOS default already separates; on Compose/CSS the two views already share the same top edge, so the constraint is a no-op there. Same root cause as common/alignTop__true. Family: gravity-default-drift.

measured drift, NOT accepted as correct: the divergence is in the DEFAULT, not in the attribute. Compose/CSS already stack a child at top/start, so declaring it changes nothing; SwiftUI's plain container centers (measured: control_View places the 200pt child at y=351..551pt of an 874pt screen), so declaring alignTop moves it. attribute_semantics gravityDefaults.defaultGravity rules the canonical default is top|start — the iOS default contradicts the ruling. Family: gravity-default-drift.

adjudicated host-shim limitation (web), NOT a converter defect: the emitted class is `disabled:bg-<name>`, and the conformance host resolves palette names through a GENERATED plain-CSS shim (`.bg-dark_red { … }`) that carries no variants — so the base utility renders and the `disabled:` variant has nothing to resolve to. A consumer whose globals.css registers the colours in `@theme` gets the variant from Tailwind itself. Re-measure if the host stops needing the shim. Family: host-shim-variant-gap.
